- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots; apply a 2–5% downward correction in subsequent days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) and price drops, model frequently undercorrects; add 1–2% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in early forecast periods (e.g., 1–3 days ahead); adjust by smoothing toward recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overpredict mid-term volatility; reduce forecast by 1–4% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.6), model often fails to capture trend reversal; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5-day highs/lows to anchor forecast.
